title: Method 2 (sorting): sort in ascending order, then return the rightmost k elements
summary: Sort the entire array in ascending order first, then take the last k elements.
context: In this example, k = 3, and the diagram has three rows from top to bottom: the input array, the sorted array, and the extracted slice. The top row shows nums = [1, 7, 6, 3, 2].
description: The first downward arrow is labeled “Sort the array,” turning the second row into [1, 2, 3, 6, 7]; the rightmost three elements 3, 6, and 7 are marked by blue borders and a brace underneath.
result: With an O(n log n) sorting algorithm, total time is O(n log n); this approach also sorts the remaining elements that do not need to be returned.

frames.title: Method 2 (sorting): sort in ascending order, then return the rightmost k elements
frames.explanation: The second downward arrow is labeled “Return the rightmost k elements,” leaving only [3, 6, 7] on the third row while discarding the smaller elements 1 and 2. Because larger values sit on the right of an ascending array, taking the last k items suffices.
